senses.gloss:
Nair-ukta^1 in the Nirukta^2 denotes a man who knows the
true etymology of words, and explains their meaning accord-
ingly. Yāska's Nirukta is the classic work of this school, and
forms a commentary on an earlier Nirukta, the so-called
Naighaṇṭuka, a glossary consisting of five collections of Vedic
words.
1) ‘One concerned with etymological
explanation’ (nir-ukta).
2) i. 12; vi. 11; xi. 19. 29. 31; xii. 10;
xiii. 9.
Cf. Weber, Indian Literature, 26, 85;
Indische Studien, 2, 39, n.; Sieg, Die
Sagenstoffc des Ṛgveda, 10-13; Muir,
Sanskrit Texts, 2^2, 165 et seq.
